title: Linearized coupled equations and gauge identities

items.title: Linearized geometric electrovacuum operator and gauge equivalence
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Assume the countable-choice background $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ carried by the stated Lorentzian geometry suppliers. Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be an oriented, time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, with metric-selected connection and orientation as in the geometric electrovac convention. In a length-coordinate chart, metric components are dimensionless and a geometric-normalized real two-form has components of unit $\mathrm{m}^{-1}$.

For a smooth real two-form $\mathcal F$, put
$$Q_{ab}(g,\mathcal F):=\mathcal F_{ac}\mathcal F_b{}^c-\frac14 g_{ab}\mathcal F_{cd}\mathcal F^{cd},$$
where all raised indices use $g^{-1}$. Its length-coordinate components have unit $\mathrm{m}^{-2}$. Fix $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ with unit $\mathrm{m}^{-2}$. An **exact geometric electrovacuum background on $U\subseteq M$** is a smooth pair $(g,\mathcal F)$ on the same open set satisfying
$$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}[g]-\Lambda g_{ab}=2Q_{ab}(g,\mathcal F),\qquad d\mathcal F=0,\qquad d(\star_g\mathcal F)=0.$$
For $\Lambda=0$ this is the geometric normalization of [[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]]. The symbol $\mathcal F$ here is geometric-normalized; it is not the SI-normalized field tensor used in [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]].

Fix such a background on $U$. A **linearized perturbation** is a pair $(h,f)$ consisting of a smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor $h$ and a smooth real two-form $f$ on $U$. Its linearized metric residual is
$$\delta E_{(g,\mathcal F)}[h,f]:=\left.\frac{d}{d\epsilon}\right|_{\epsilon=0}\bigl(\operatorname{Ric}[g_\epsilon]-\Lambda g_\epsilon-2Q(g_\epsilon,\mathcal F_\epsilon)\bigr),$$
and its linearized Maxwell residuals are
$$df,\qquad d\,\delta(\star\mathcal F),\qquad \delta(\star\mathcal F):=\left.\frac{d}{d\epsilon}\right|_{\epsilon=0}\star_{g_\epsilon}\mathcal F_\epsilon.$$
Here $g_\epsilon=g+\epsilon h+O(\epsilon^2)$ and $\mathcal F_\epsilon=\mathcal F+\epsilon f+O(\epsilon^2)$ are smooth local families on the fixed domain, with dimensionless parameter $\epsilon$. The derivatives are the coordinatewise derivatives of these smooth finite-jet operators; the chain rule makes them depend only on $(h,f)$, not on the higher-order parts of the chosen families. The **linearized electrovacuum system** is the homogeneous system $\delta E_{(g,\mathcal F)}[h,f]=0$, $df=0$, and $d\,\delta(\star\mathcal F)=0$.

For a smooth vector field $X$, let $\Phi_\epsilon$ be its local flow and define the **pure gauge perturbation** by $(h,f)=\left.\frac{d}{d\epsilon}\right|_0(\Phi_\epsilon^*g,\Phi_\epsilon^*\mathcal F)$. A **parameter perturbation** is the derivative of a smooth one-parameter family of exact geometric electrovacuum backgrounds on one common open domain. Neither definition asserts that every solution of the linearized system is pure gauge or is a parameter perturbation.

For a local diffeomorphism $\Phi:V\to W$ and a covariant $r$-tensor $T$ on $W$, its pullback is $(\Phi^*T)_p(v_1,\ldots,v_r):=T_{\Phi(p)}(D\Phi_pv_1,\ldots,D\Phi_pv_r)$; this fixes the pullback convention in the pure-gauge definition.

If a potential perturbation $a\in\Omega^1(V)$ is chosen on an open set $V\subseteq U$ with $f=da$, then $a$ and $a+d\chi$ represent the same field-strength perturbation for every smooth scalar $\chi$ on $V$. No global exactness of $f$ or global potential is assumed.

references.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Chapter 6 and Chapter 7, equations (7.106)–(7.113)
references.locator: Chapter 6, PDF pp. 149–158 (printed pp. 142–151), gives the background-field perturbation and infinitesimal diffeomorphism gauge law; Chapter 7, PDF pp. 208–209 (printed pp. 201–202), gives the coupled Einstein–Maxwell equations and Reissner–Nordström family. The flat-background formulas and the notes' Gaussian normalization are not imported as curved-background or SI conventions.

references.title: Elena Giorgi, The linear stability of Reissner–Nordström spacetime for small charge, arXiv:1904.04926v2 (2020)
references.locator: Sections 1 and 6.1–6.2, PDF pp. 1–4 and 43–55: the coupled Einstein–Maxwell perturbation equations, residual pure-gauge solutions, and the linearized Kerr–Newman parameter family. The paper's decay theorem has additional small-charge, asymptotically flat and Bondi-gauge hypotheses and is not asserted here.

items.title: Variation of the Lorentzian Hodge map and the linearized Maxwell equation
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $g_\epsilon=g+\epsilon h+O(\epsilon^2)$ be a smooth variation of an oriented Lorentzian metric on a four-manifold, and let $\omega_\epsilon=\omega+\epsilon\tau+O(\epsilon^2)$ be a smooth variation of a $k$-form, $0\le k\le4$. Define $h_a{}^b:=g^{bc}h_{ac}$, $\operatorname{tr}_g h:=g^{ab}h_{ab}$, and
$$\bigl(h^\sharp\!\cdot\omega\bigr)_{a_1\ldots a_k}:=\sum_{j=1}^k h_{a_j}{}^b\omega_{a_1\ldots a_{j-1}b a_{j+1}\ldots a_k},$$
with $h^\sharp\!\cdot\omega:=0$ for $k=0$. Then
$$\left.\frac{d}{d\epsilon}\right|_0\star_{g_\epsilon}\omega_\epsilon=\star_g\left(\tau+\frac12(\operatorname{tr}_g h)\omega-h^\sharp\!\cdot\omega\right).$$
In particular, for the geometric background $\mathcal F$ and perturbation $f$ of [[def-emg-fx-linearized-electrovac]],
$$\delta(\star\mathcal F)=\star_g\left(f+\frac12(\operatorname{tr}_g h)\mathcal F-h^\sharp\!\cdot\mathcal F\right).$$
If $(h,f)$ satisfies the linearized Maxwell equation, then $d\,\delta(\star\mathcal F)=0$; this last condition is exactly the derivative of $d(\star_{g_\epsilon}\mathcal F_\epsilon)=0$, not a consequence of the variation formula alone.

references.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Chapter 1, equations (1.87)–(1.93)
references.locator: PDF pp. 30–31 (printed pp. 23–24): Hodge star from the metric and orientation, its Lorentzian signature factor, and the exterior-form Maxwell equations. The variation formula below is derived locally by differentiating the component definition.

items.title: Pure-gauge and exact-family perturbations solve the linearized electrovacuum system
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement: Let $(g,\mathcal F)$ be a smooth exact geometric electrovacuum background on an open domain $U$ as in [[def-emg-fx-linearized-electrovac]]. If $X$ is a smooth vector field on $U$ and $\Phi_\epsilon:V\to U$ is an orientation-preserving local flow it generates, where $V\subseteq U$ is open, $\Phi_0$ is the inclusion, and $\partial_\epsilon\Phi_\epsilon=X\circ\Phi_\epsilon$ wherever defined, then the pure-gauge perturbation $(\dot\Phi_0^*g,\dot\Phi_0^*\mathcal F)$ solves the linearized electrovacuum system on every common flow domain. More generally, let $\lambda\mapsto(g_\lambda,\mathcal F_\lambda)$ be a smooth one-parameter family of exact backgrounds on a common domain, with every member satisfying the equations for one fixed value of $\Lambda$. Its derivative at any parameter value solves the linearized system at that member. In the $\Lambda=0$ sector, fixed-domain Reissner–Nordström and Kerr–Newman parameter families provide stationary parameter modes, meaning that their displayed metric and field components are independent of $x^0$, on exterior domains admitted by their verification results, when the parameters vary in an interval on which one such domain remains common. These conclusions do not classify the kernel of the linearized operator or determine which of its solutions arise as derivatives of exact solution families (integrable perturbations).

references.title: Elena Giorgi, The linear stability of Reissner–Nordström spacetime for small charge, arXiv:1904.04926v2 (2020), Sections 6.1–6.2
references.locator: PDF pp. 43–55: pure-gauge perturbations and the six-parameter linearized Kerr–Newman family. The proof here uses diffeomorphism naturality and exact-family differentiation, not Giorgi's decay theorem.

references.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Chapter 6, equations (6.10)–(6.14)
references.locator: PDF pp. 151–153 (printed pp. 144–146): background-spacetime perturbations, infinitesimal coordinate gauge transformations and invariance of linearized curvature in the flat-background case.

items.title: Finite-slab energy control and subsidiary propagation for the linearized electrovacuum system
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $T>0$ and let $(g,\mathcal F)$ be a smooth exact geometric electrovacuum background on the product collar $[-T,T]\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, where $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}:=(\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z)^3$; exactness means $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}[g]-\Lambda g_{ab}=2Q_{ab}(g,\mathcal F)$ and $d\mathcal F=d(\star_g\mathcal F)=0$, with $Q_{ab}(g,\mathcal F):=\mathcal F_{ac}\mathcal F_b{}^c-\tfrac14g_{ab}\mathcal F_{cd}\mathcal F^{cd}$. Here $x^0=t$ is a length coordinate, $n=\partial_t$ is the future unit normal, and
$$g=-dt^2+\gamma_{ij}(t,\theta)d\theta^i d\theta^j$$
with $\gamma$ a smooth positive spatial metric. The fixed cosmological parameter $\Lambda$ has units $\mathrm{m}^{-2}$. Fix the harmonic reference metric $\bar g$ to equal the background and define $H^a[g_\epsilon]:=g_\epsilon^{bc}(\Gamma^a{}_{bc}[g_\epsilon]-\bar\Gamma^a{}_{bc})$, with $H_b[g_\epsilon]:=g_{\epsilon bc}H^c[g_\epsilon]$. Thus the background gauge vector vanishes and the linearized reduced metric equation is the derivative of $\operatorname{Ric}[g_\epsilon]-\nabla^{g_\epsilon}_{(a}H_{b)}[g_\epsilon]-\Lambda g_{\epsilon ab}-2Q_{ab}(g_\epsilon,\mathcal F_\epsilon)=0$. Let $L_0>0$ be the fixed spatial length scale and, on the covering space $\mathbb R^3$, write $X^i=L_0\theta^i$. Use the global frame descended from the standard frame of $\mathbb R^3$ on $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, denoted $\partial_{\theta^i}$, and let $(\mathsf e_1,\mathsf e_2,\mathsf e_3)$ be its Gram–Schmidt orthonormalization for $\gamma$, oriented so that $(n,\mathsf e_1,\mathsf e_2,\mathsf e_3)$ is positive for the spacetime orientation; write $\varepsilon_{123}=1$. For the geometric-normalized two-form perturbation $f=\dot{\mathcal F}_0$ from [[def-emg-fx-linearized-electrovac]], define
$$e_i:=f(\mathsf e_i,n),\qquad b_i:=\frac12\varepsilon_i{}^{jk}f(\mathsf e_j,\mathsf e_k),$$
where indices on $\varepsilon_{ijk}$ are raised with $\delta_{ij}$. The variation parameter is dimensionless, so these components have the geometric field-strength units of $\mathcal F$ (length-coordinate components have unit $\mathrm{m}^{-1}$). The first-order state is the $56$-component periodic array $u=(h_{ab},p_{ab},q_{abi},e_i,b_i)$, where $h$ is the metric perturbation, $p_{ab}=\bar\nabla_0h_{ab}$, and $q_{abi}=\bar\nabla_i h_{ab}$. For a periodic $56$-component array, define
$$\widehat u(\ell):=(2\pi)^{-3}\int_{[0,2\pi)^3}u(\theta)e^{-i\ell\cdot\theta}\,d\theta,\qquad \|u\|_{H^k}^2:=\sum_{\ell\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+|\ell|^2)^k|\widehat u(\ell)|^2.$$
Write $x=\theta$ in the system below and absorb the fixed factor $L_0^{-1}$ from $\partial_{X^i}=L_0^{-1}\partial_{\theta^i}$ into its spatial matrices. For a smooth linearized perturbation state $u:[-T,T]\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\to\mathbb R^{56}$ and smooth source $s:[-T,T]\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\to\mathbb R^{56}$, write the inhomogeneous first-order system in the chosen trivialization as
$$A^0(t,x)\partial_tu+\sum_{i=1}^3 A^i(t,x)\partial_i u+C(t,x)u=s(t,x),$$
where $A^0,A^1,A^2,A^3,C:[-T,T]\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\to\mathbb R^{56\times56}$ are smooth periodic matrix fields, each $A^i$ and $A^0$ is symmetric, and constants $0<a\le b<\infty$ satisfy $aI\le A^0(t,x)\le bI$ throughout the slab. In the normal-flow chart, the harmonic metric reduction has time matrix $\operatorname{diag}(I,I,\gamma^{ij}I)$ and symmetric spatial matrices by [F1], while the six Maxwell field-strength variables have time matrix $I_6$ and symmetric spatial matrices by [F2]. When the Maxwell equations are linearized, derivatives of the perturbed lapse, frame and spatial metric occur through $p_{ab}$ and $q_{abi}$, which are components of the state and hence contribute to $C u$, not to spatial derivatives of the state. The variation of the Maxwell stress in the metric equation is algebraic in $(h,f)$ by [F3]. Thus the full principal matrices are the direct sums of the metric and Maxwell principal matrices, and the remaining couplings are smooth zeroth-order terms. Compactness of the slab then supplies uniform positive bounds for $A^0$.

For every integer $k\ge0$, define
$$\mathcal E_k(t):=\sum_{|\alpha|\le k}\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}(\partial^\alpha u)^T A^0(t,x)\partial^\alpha u\,dx.$$
There is a constant $C_k$, depending only on $a,b,T$ and the coefficient derivatives through order $k+1$, such that
$$\|u(t)\|_{H^k}\le C_k e^{C_k|t|}\left(\|u(0)\|_{H^k}+\int_{\min(0,t)}^{\max(0,t)}\|s(\tau)\|_{H^k}\,d\tau\right),\qquad |t|\le T.$$
This is a finite-time conditional estimate, not an existence theorem or a global decay statement.

For the unforced linearized system, the Maxwell subsidiary constraints are the spatial restrictions of $df$ and $d\,\delta(\star\mathcal F)$ to a slice. If the normal-slot linearized Maxwell evolution equations hold and both initial restrictions vanish, they remain zero on the slab. Define $\dot H^a:=\left.\frac{d}{d\epsilon}\right|_0H^a[g_\epsilon]$ and $\dot H_b:=g_{bc}\dot H^c$ at the background; since $H^a[g]=0$, $\dot H_b$ is also the variation of $H_b[g_\epsilon]$. If the linearized reduced Einstein and Maxwell equations hold and $\dot H_b=\partial_t\dot H_b=0$ initially, then $\dot H^a=0$ throughout the slab. These are the Maxwell Gauss and harmonic-gauge subsidiary identities; no decay of the physical perturbation is asserted.

references.title: Helmut Friedrich and Alan Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, Living Reviews in Relativity 3 (2000), article 1, arXiv:gr-qc/0002074, Section 3.1
references.locator: PDF pp. 22–31: symmetric first-order systems, the energy identity, higher-order commutator estimates, and the distinction between local energy control and existence/continuation conclusions. The inhomogeneous Duhamel estimate and the exact linearized constraints are proved locally here.

references.title: Elena Giorgi, The linear stability of Reissner–Nordström spacetime for small charge, arXiv:1904.04926v2 (2020), Sections 1 and 6
references.locator: PDF pp. 1–4 and 43–55: the coupled metric/electromagnetic perturbation system, pure-gauge and parameter modes, and the substantially stronger asymptotically flat decay theorem. Only the local perturbation conventions and its explicit limitations inform this finite-slab result.

title: Linearized coupled equations and gauge identities — Examples

items.title: A stationary Reissner–Nordström charge mode does not decay to zero
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Work in the $\Lambda=0$ specialization of the linearized geometric electrovacuum system. Fix $M>0$, $q_0>0$, $R_0>4M$, and a length $\ell_*>0$. Set the dimensionless parameter radius $\epsilon:=q_0/(2\ell_*)$ and $q(\lambda):=q_0+\lambda\ell_*$. Then $q(\lambda)>q_0/2>0$ for $|\lambda|<\epsilon$. On the fixed exterior $U=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times(R_0,\infty)\times S^2$, put
$$f_\lambda(r)=1-\frac{2M}{r}+\frac{q(\lambda)^2}{r^2},\qquad g_\lambda=-f_\lambda(dx^0)^2+f_\lambda^{-1}dr^2+r^2\gamma_{S^2},\qquad \mathcal F_\lambda=-\frac{q(\lambda)}{r^2}dx^0\wedge dr.$$
Then $h:=\partial_\lambda g_\lambda|_0$ and $f:=\partial_\lambda\mathcal F_\lambda|_0$ form a smooth stationary solution of the linearized geometric electrovacuum system at $(g_0,\mathcal F_0)$. Its electromagnetic perturbation is nonzero and its electric-flux variation through every outward coordinate sphere $S_r$ is $\partial_\lambda q_e(S_r)|_0=\ell_*$. Thus this exact mode does not tend to zero in time at fixed $r$; an unqualified claim that every linearized component decays to zero without retaining or subtracting parameter modes is false.

references.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Chapter 7, equations (7.106)–(7.113)
references.locator: PDF pp. 208–210 (printed pp. 201–203): the exact dyonic Reissner–Nordström field, charge parameter and electric flux convention. The geometric normalization is that of the local supplier.

references.title: Elena Giorgi, The linear stability of Reissner–Nordström spacetime for small charge, arXiv:1904.04926v2 (2020), Section 6.2
references.locator: PDF pp. 51–55: parameter derivatives give non-radiating linearized Kerr–Newman modes; the local example below computes one electric-charge mode on a fixed exterior chart.
